sections.h2: What helps a Gloucester Township house sell quickly
sections.html:
Speed in this township comes from getting three items in order early: the fire-district certificate, written payoffs for loans and taxes, and an asking price based on recent nearby sales. Gloucester Township lies in Camden County, with an estimated 67,085 residents in 2025. The 2020 census placed it 22nd of New Jersey's 565 municipalities.

About 73.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with a typical value of $277,800. A tired house competes with polished listings here, so some owners take an as-is cash offer rather than paying for repairs, open houses and a buyer's loan approval.

The township covers 22.95 square miles of land. Communities inside it include Blackwood, Glendora, Grenloch, Chews Landing, Erial, Glen Oaks, Lambs Terrace and Turkey Foot, and a listing should name the one that matches your street.

One useful first step is to pull your tax bill and any loan statements and line them up beside the closing date you want. If the house will go to a cash buyer, ask the buyer to confirm in writing who orders the fire-district certificate and who pays its fee. Those two decisions are where as-is sales most often slip.

Also decide early how you will hand over the keys. If tenants live in the house, a buyer will want to know the lease terms and whether the unit will be empty at closing, and that should be written into the contract.

sections.h2: Numbers that should guide your price
sections.html:
In 2025 the typical home carried a $7,920 tax bill, and the 710 homes in the state's sales study averaged $338,576.

The 2025 general tax rate is 4.179 per $100 and the effective rate is 2.703. Sales averaged about $149,000 over the average assessment, which is why recent closings, not the tax card, should set your price.

The fire district serving your street handles it, because the township is split into several fire districts. Fire District No. 4's Bureau of Fire Prevention posts the application form for this certification and accepts inspection requests by phone or email.

To find your district, search your street address in the township's property tax lookup and read the Special Taxing Districts line on the record. FIRE DISTRICT=F04 means District No. 4. The state wants the certificate in place before a one-family or two-family house is sold. Once issued it lasts six months, so time the inspection near your closing.

Alarm requirements can vary with a property's age and layout, and a failed inspection brings a list of fixes and a re-inspection. Fix the listed items quickly, since a re-check is what gets the certificate issued. Before listing, ask the township construction office if any further resale paperwork applies.

sections.h2: How does the tax office handle a sale?
sections.html:
Taxes are billed in four installments, due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, each with the longest 10-day grace period state law permits. Overdue balances earn 8 percent yearly interest up to $1,500 and 18 percent past that, and a balance above $10,000 still open at year end adds a 6 percent penalty. Current-year taxes unpaid after November 11 can go to tax sale before December 30, and anyone paying in that window must use cash or certified funds.

Two $250 deductions exist, one for qualifying seniors and disabled residents and one for veteran owners. Bill dates can move if the tax levy certification is late, so get a written payoff figure before closing.

An assessment appeal goes to the Camden County Board of Taxation, due by 4:00 p.m. on April 1 (May 1 after a town revaluation). The $25 filing fee for assessments from $150,000 to $500,000 covers the township's average residential assessment. Keep paying taxes during an appeal, or it can be dismissed.

sections.h2: What a seller pays at closing
sections.html:
Your loan payoff and the state Realty Transfer Fee are normally the biggest costs. For prices at or below $350,000 the fee starts at $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, and it is the seller's to pay when the deed is recorded. Ask your closing attorney for the exact figure before you sign.

  • Transfer fee, from the state's rate table.
  • Payoff of the mortgage, credit line or tax lien.
  • Certificate fee charged by the fire district.
  • The GIT/REP-3 residency certification attached to the deed.

Deeds are recorded by the Camden County Clerk, 520 Market Street in Camden, which accepts electronic recording. Sellers living out of state prepay at least 2 percent of the price as Gross Income Tax unless an assurance on the GIT/REP-3 applies.

Local public schools run from prekindergarten through eighth grade. High schoolers attend Highland Regional in Blackwood, Timber Creek Regional in Erial or Triton Regional in Runnemede, assigned by address within the Black Horse Pike Regional School District.

The Atlantic City Expressway clips the southwest corner, Routes 42 and 168 run through the west, and County Routes 534 and 544 cover the center and the northern edge. NJ Transit's 400 bus reaches Philadelphia, and the 403 and 459 serve local trips.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or a house with liens
sections.html:
Landlords register through a Landlord Identity Registration form on the township's downloads page, so confirm yours is current before listing. Renters live in about 27 percent of homes at a typical rent of $1,592, so a tenant-occupied sale is nothing unusual. The fire certificate also applies to a lease or change of occupancy.

Liens do not block a sale as long as the price covers every payoff. That includes a mortgage, credit line, tax lien or pending foreclosure. Ask each lender and the tax collector for written figures, because tax sale charges add fees beyond the posted tax total. Have those numbers before you accept an offer, so the closing statement holds no surprises. On the day of closing the attorney or title company pays off each lender, records the deed with the transfer fee and GIT/REP form, and sends you the remaining proceeds.

faqs.q: Does Gloucester Township require a resale certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: The certificate you need covers smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and comes from the fire district for your address. The construction office can say whether anything else applies.

faqs.q: How can I tell which fire district my house is in?
faqs.a: Search your street address in the township's property tax lookup and read the Special Taxing Districts line. F04 means Fire District No. 4.

faqs.q: What are the Gloucester Township tax due dates?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, each with a 10-day grace period. Late balances accrue interest, and unpaid current-year taxes can go to tax sale after November 11.

faqs.q: By when must I appeal a Gloucester Township assessment?
faqs.a: Before 4:00 p.m. on April 1, or on May 1 if the town did a revaluation or reassessment. The county Board of Taxation sits at 509 Lakeland Road in Blackwood and offers a summary hearing with no appearance needed.

faqs.q: May I sell a Gloucester Township house with liens or a foreclosure pending?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sale price covers every payoff. Request written figures from each lender and the tax collector, because tax sale charges add fees on top of the posted tax total.
